changes: p3: name normalized to 'Jitāmitramalladeva' (regnal name); 'sumatijaya' is the standard Bhaktapur royal epithet prefixed to the name, so it now goes in titles and is not part of the name
p4 Bhāgirāma: role changed from 'other' to 'minister' (medium confidence). 'pradhānāṅga' is the Bhaktapur office title of the chief minister, and '-yā velaśa' means 'in the time/tenure of'
Added relation p2 under_reign_of p3 and p4 servant_of p3; kept p2 wrote_for p3
Notes expanded: catalogue scribe field, the Nevārī reading of 'cocakā', the place, and the eulogistic verse

notes: The era is not named, but year 803 under Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur (r. c. 1673–1696) fits NS, so NS 803 Māgha = c. January 1683 CE. The catalogue lists Bhāgirāma Pradhānāṅga as a scribe, but the colophon names only Ratnākara as scribe ('śrīratnākareṇa likhitaṃ'). The Nevārī says the king had the book written ('cocakā' = causative of 'co-', to write) 'bhāgirāmapradhānāṅgayā velaśa', i.e. in the time or under the supervision of Bhāgirāma Pradhānāṅga. 'Pradhānāṅga' is a ministerial title, so Bhāgirāma is taken as the minister in charge, possibly the overseer of the copying. No place is stated; Bhaktapur is likely because of the king, but this is not certain. The bhujaṅgaprayāta verse praising Jitāmitramalla is eulogistic and names no further persons. The final sentence is a request to others to look after the book carefully.
